analysis: Hairy cell leukemia is a rare type of chronic B-cell leukemia characterized by the presence of abnormal B lymphocytes with 'hairy' projections. The disease typically presents with pancytopenia due to bone marrow infiltration, leading to a reduction in all types of blood cells, and splenomegaly due to the accumulation of these abnormal cells in the spleen. Lymphocytosis, especially at levels greater than 50,000 lymphocytes/microL, is not characteristic of hairy cell leukemia, as the condition often results in decreased lymphocyte counts. The disease is a B-cell neoplasm, so it does not present with T lymphoid line markers. Additionally, skin manifestations such as exfoliative erythroderma, plaques, and skin tumors are not associated with hairy cell leukemia. Therefore, the most characteristic clinical-biological features of hairy cell leukemia are pancytopenia and splenomegaly.
